head: 847434e03cfc5f508968260570f69366500958dc

non_issues.claim: own_host_header should normalise the Host (lowercase, strip a trailing dot or whitespace, accept [::1]:<port> or *.localhost) because browsers can send those spellings; the exact comparison is too strict
non_issues.why_not: Deliberate: the helper must be byte-identical to the seven copies it replaces and admit no new spelling (docs/plans/2026-10-18-dedupe-cleanup.md:75-82: 'no new spelling ([::1], a trailing dot, case) is admitted'); the docstring at jarvis/config.py:117-121 says admitting another spelling loosens the DNS-rebinding guard. The old copies were the same exact tuple membership test.

non_issues.claim: projects.is_owner's Origin branch compares origin == f'http://{host}' without checking the Host through own_host_header, so a forged Host with a matching Origin is treated as the owner
non_issues.why_not: Unchanged by this diff and covered upstream: hud_api.check_origin runs on every request before any route (jarvis/v2/daemon.py:2520-2521) and refuses any Host that is not 127.0.0.1:<port>/localhost:<port> ('untrusted Host'); the is_owner docstring (jarvis/v2/projects.py:146-151) records this layering and says to keep all three checks. own_host_header_check's Sites tests patch check_origin out precisely to show the per-route checks still refuse (tests/v2/own_host_header_check.py:186-262).

non_issues.claim: check_origin takes the port from handler.server.server_address[1] while the other sites use daemon.face_port, so the helper is called inconsistently and one of them checks the wrong port
non_issues.why_not: Each site keeps its own port choice on purpose (docs/plans/2026-10-18-dedupe-cleanup.md:79-81: 'some take a different port (face_port, hud=); keep that'): check_origin also guards the preview listener, whose own port is the right one (daemon.py:450 preview_only, :2521). The pre-diff code used exactly the same ports at every site.

non_issues.claim: The Sites tests patch jarvis.v2.hud_api.check_origin, but the daemon holds its own reference, so the patch has no effect and the per-route tests pass vacuously on check_origin's refusal
non_issues.why_not: The daemon imports check_origin inside the handler on every request (jarvis/v2/daemon.py:2520 'from .hud_api import check_origin'), so the patch takes effect. Verified by mutation: replacing the own_host_header call with True at browser/routes.py, vex.py, devservers.py, terminals.py or daemon.py (approvals hud=) each makes the matching Sites test fail with 7 failures (8 for daemon), and is_owner's mutation makes owner_read_check IsOwnerClauses fail.

non_issues.claim: A pure refactor's tests cannot fail without the change, so the new test file proves nothing about the seven sites
non_issues.why_not: The plan asks for a unit table plus a per-site mutation proof (docs/plans/2026-10-18-dedupe-cleanup.md:84-89). Mutating any single site's check to True makes a test fail (own_host_header_check for routes/vex/devservers/terminals/approvals and check_origin; owner_read_check for is_owner), so every replaced site is pinned.

non_issues.claim: own_host_header crashes or misbehaves on a missing/None Host value
non_issues.why_not: Every caller passes headers.get('Host', '') so a missing header is '' and fails; None is also just not in the tuple and returns False. Both are in the unit table (tests/v2/own_host_header_check.py:89-90) and pass.

non_issues.claim: Treating the Host header as proof of the owner (approvals hud= flag, vex/devservers owner checks) is spoofable by any local process that sends Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>
non_issues.why_not: Documented scope: these checks are a DNS-rebinding guard for browser pages, not a boundary against a program running as the owner (jarvis/v2/projects.py:150-152 'A program running as the owner can send any of these headers; this was never a boundary against one'). Behaviour is unchanged by this refactor.

notes: Verified clean. All six listed suites pass on the head (own_host_header_check 10, browser_routes_check 36, hud_backend_check 92, terminal_check 91, vex_check 153, owner_read_check 18; owner_read_check needs PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH when HOME is temporary). Grep finds no remaining inline Host tuple under jarvis/v2. Per-site mutation (each own_host_header call -> True) is caught at all seven sites. No later commit on main touches own_host_header. No touched file is in SELF_PROTECTED (jarvis/tools/files.py).
